title: DNS: Added new statistics called Query-Response.
description:
- This re-categorizes existing statistic and adds few more categories.
- It is enabled by default but could be disabled via its preference.
- Queried DNS names could also be listed when enabled via a preference.

For Query
- From: IP Addresses
- Opcodes: Uses existing statistics (Standard query, ...).
- Kind: Recursion Desired or Iteration Desired
- Types: Uses existing statistics (A, AAA,HTTPS,...).
- Labels: Extends existing 4+ levels to 9+ plus extracts-n-shows the under
the query.
- Payload: Bucketed from zero to > 64KB (using power of 2).
- Servicing: Answered, Unaswered along with Retransmissions.

For Response
- TTL: For each answer (answers, authorities and additionals) bucketed from
a minute to > year but without cumulative total for TTL node itself.
- Servicing: Uses existing statistics.
- Rcodes: Uses existing statistics (No error, No such name).
- Payload: Bucketed from zero to > 64KB (using power of 2).
- Kind: Authoritative or Non-Authoritative
- From: IP Addresses
- Authorities, Answers, Additionals: Number of responses bucketed from zero
to > 4K (using power of 2).

Can you rebase your change ?

When I attempted to do so using [fixing-merge-errors](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/wikis/Development/SubmittingPatches#fixing-merge-errors), after resolving merge conflicts and `git rebase --continue`, I was unable to use `git commit --amend` and a new commit id was seen in the git log for my branch. Is this expected or am I missing a step here? Because as per the link, it says _"you don't want to generate a new commit and new review"_
you need to make a git push -f after (it is not a problem if there is a new commit sha, you need to have only one commit)

It looks like the Average and Min/Max Val doesn't work.

![Screenshot_2024-03-08_at_08.43.08](/uploads/cc548eddea1c7a0fff306bd4b70bfe40/Screenshot_2024-03-08_at_08.43.08.png)
That seems to be the case for all statistics dialogs, for me at least. Looks like that broke at some point.

Stats tree has to be called a special way to do averages, with `stats_tree_tick_range` instead of `tick_node`.

The only dialog that uses it is the Packet Lengths one, and it works there.

Possibly it shouldn't be displayed for any dialog that doesn't use it, because it's confusing.

However, this dialog is a case where it should be used, because those are ranges, not single values.
